test_title: SSC Selection Post 2024 (Higher Secondary Level) Official Paper (Held On: 20 Jun, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament (Amendment) ordinance, 2020 reduced the salary of Members of Parliament by. _______ for a period of one year commencing from 1 April 2020 to meet the exigencies arising out of COVID-19.
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.3**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **30%** reduction in the salary of Members of Parliament was stipulated by the Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament (Amendment) Ordinance, 2020.
 
• This reduction was implemented for a period of **one year** commencing from **1 April 2020**.
 
• The decision was made to meet the **exigencies arising out of COVID-19**.
 
• In addition to the salary reduction, the government also amended the **Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS)** to suspend its operation for two years and use the funds for managing health services and the adverse impact of COVID-19 in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954** governs the salaries, allowances, and pensions of MPs in India.
 
• Amendments to this Act can be made through ordinances or legislative procedures by the Parliament of India.
 
• The **President of India** promulgated the ordinance on the advice of the Union Cabinet under **Article 123** of the Constitution of India.
 
• During the COVID-19 pandemic, the government took several measures to reallocate resources and manage the financial burden caused by the crisis.
 
• Such measures are crucial for ensuring that funds are available for **public health and welfare** during emergencies.
